entities.summary:
Dou Xian was a Chinese general and consort kin of the Eastern Han dynasty, famous for destroying the Xiongnu nomadic empire. A member of the powerful Dou family, he rose to prominence during the reign of Emperor Ling of Han (168-189 CE) and played a key role in the dynasty's military campaigns against the Xiongnu. Dou Xian's exploits were documented in the Records of the Three Kingdoms, a historical text that showcases his bravery and military prowess.

Dou Xian's legacy extends beyond his military achievements, as he helped to establish the Dou family as a dominant force in Eastern Han politics. His actions had a profound impact on the regional dynamics of Northern China, shaping the course of the Xiongnu's decline and the rise of new powers in the region.

Despite his significant contributions to Chinese history, Dou Xian's life and legacy remain somewhat shadowed by the more famous figures of the Three Kingdoms period. Nevertheless, his story serves as a testament to the enduring power of military leadership and the importance of strategic alliances in shaping the course of human history.
